Author: Binbin <binloveplay1314@qq.com>
Date:   Fri Aug 23 16:21:53 2024 +0800

    Fix CLUSTER SETSLOT block and unblock error when all replicas are down (#879)
    
    In CLUSTER SETSLOT propagation logic, if the replicas are down, the
    client will get block during command processing and then unblock
    with `NOREPLICAS Not enough good replicas to write`.
    
    The reason is that all replicas are down (or some are down), but
    myself->num_replicas is including all replicas, so the client will
    get block and always get timeout.
    
    We should only wait for those online replicas, otherwise the waiting
    propagation will always timeout since there are not enough replicas.
    The admin can easily check if there are replicas that are down for an
    extended period of time. If they decide to move forward anyways, we
    should not block it. If a replica  failed right before the replication and
    was not included in the replication, it would also unlikely win the election.
    
    Signed-off-by: Binbin <binloveplay1314@qq.com>
    Co-authored-by: Ping Xie <pingxie@google.com>

1. Primary calling blockClientForReplicaAck, waiting its replica.

+
+start_cluster 4 4 {tags {external:skip cluster} overrides {cluster-node-timeout 1000 cluster-migration-barrier 999}} {
+    test "valkey-cli make source node ignores NOREPLICAS error when doing the last CLUSTER SETSLOT" {
+        R 3 config set cluster-allow-replica-migration no
+        R 7 config set cluster-allow-replica-migration yes
+
+        # Record the current primary node, server 7 will be migrated later.
+        set old_primary_ip [lindex [R 7 role] 1]
+        set old_primary_port [lindex [R 7 role] 2]
+
+        # Move slot 0 from primary 3 to primary 0.
+        set addr "[srv 0 host]:[srv 0 port]"
+        set myid [R 3 CLUSTER MYID]
+        set code [catch {
+            exec src/valkey-cli {*}[valkeycli_tls_config "./tests"] --cluster rebalance $addr --cluster-weight $myid=0
+        } result]
+        if {$code != 0} {
+            fail "valkey-cli --cluster rebalance returns non-zero exit code, output below:\n$result"
+        }
+
+        wait_for_cluster_propagation
+        wait_for_cluster_state "ok"
+
+        # Make sure server 3 is still a primary and has no replicas.
+        assert_equal [s -3 role] {master}
+        assert_equal [lindex [R 3 role] 2] {}
+
+        # And server 7 becomes a replica of another primary.
+        set new_primary_ip [lindex [R 7 role] 1]
+        set new_primary_port [lindex [R 7 role] 2]
+        assert_equal [s -7 role] {slave}
+        assert_not_equal "$old_primary_ip:$old_primary_port" "new_primary_ip:new_primary_port"
+    }
+} my_slot_allocation cluster_allocate_replicas ;# start_cluster

part.text:
The fix is complete and validated.

**Root cause:** Since the primary now pre-replicates `CLUSTER SETSLOT` to its replicas while blocking the client on replica acks (`blockClientForReplicaAck`), a replica can migrate away to another primary during that block, so the source primary never receives the ack and the client is unblocked with a `NOREPLICAS` error. Since the topology change eventually propagates itself, valkey-cli can safely ignore this error when informing the source node.

**Fix** (matches upstream PR valkey-io/valkey#928): in `clusterManagerMoveSlot` (src/valkey-cli.c:5125), `"NOREPLICAS"` was added to the list of acceptable errors when sending the final `CLUSTER SETSLOT <slot> NODE <target>` to the source node, alongside the existing "Please use SETSLOT only with masters/primaries" and "UNBLOCKED" exceptions.

**Validation** (all in the testbed container):
- `unit/cluster/replica-migration` — passes, including the FAIL_TO_PASS test "valkey-cli make source node ignores NOREPLICAS error when doing the last CLUSTER SETSLOT"
- `unit/cluster/slot-migration`, `unit/cluster/cli`, `unit/cluster/misc`, `unit/cluster/multi-slot-operations` — all pass

(Initial repeated failures were environmental — stray test-server processes from aborted runs starved the 50s setup convergence window; after cleanup, everything passes consistently.)
